# SESSION ADDENDUM 3 — June 16, 2026 — ARTICULATED URDF DEPLOYED, SETUP/COMMISSIONING WIZARD, CELL MODEL, COLLISION DETECTION, LOCAL-VS-API PERCEPTION STRATEGY
*(Appended in full. Nothing above this line was removed. This is the June 16 working session, executed largely through Claude Code running ON THE JETSON HOST — not inside the cobot_ros container; the dashboard runs as systemd `roboai-dashboard.service` as User=teddy on the host, serving on :8080.)*

## 15. ARTICULATED S10-140 URDF — MESHES DEPLOYED FROM SOLIDWORKS (the §10/§14 PENDING items now actioned)

### 15a. SolidWorks fully-articulated assembly → 7 per-link GLB meshes
The user has SolidWorks part + assembly files for the S10-140; the assembly is fully movable (every joint articulates). DECISION on workflow: export each link as its own GLB by hiding all other components, one export per link. **7 link meshes** produced (note: this session used a 7-file naming scheme — base + 6 moving links — distinct from the "8 links" wording in §10a; the operative deployed set is these 7):
- `link0_base.glb` (188KB / 192724 bytes)
- `link1_shoulder.glb` (42KB / 43096)
- `link2_upper_arm.glb` (257KB / 263624)
- `link3_forearm.glb` (152KB / 156136)
- `link4_wrist1.glb` (94KB / 96256)
- `link5_wrist2.glb` (94KB / 96236)
- `link6_flange.glb` (247KB / 252216)

### 15b. Transfer method — SCP from Windows laptop to Jetson (NOT upload to Claude)
KEY OPERATIONAL FACT: meshes must live ON THE JETSON so the dashboard serves them; they were NOT to be uploaded into the chat. Path used: `scp <file> teddy@192.168.1.246:/home/teddy/cobot_ws/models/robots/estun_s10-140/links/`.
- The links dir ALREADY contained same-named GLBs plus `_lite` variants (pre-existing before the user arrived); SCP overwrites silently — a backup (`links.bak`) was taken first via `cp -r`.
- `/opt/cobot/models/robot` is a SYMLINK to that links dir; the dashboard serves the files at `/robot/links/{filename}` (also referenced in the URDF as `package://robot_description/links/...`). New files drop in transparently on page reload — no rebuild needed for the meshes themselves (Python unchanged, Vite doesn't bundle the GLBs).
- **Windows-path gotcha resolved:** the Windows username was `Laptop` (prompt `C:\Users\Laptop>`), NOT `Teddy`/`THEODORE` (the OneDrive display name THEODORE - Personal misled early attempts). Correct source path: `C:\Users\Laptop\Downloads\`. Confirmed with `dir C:\Users\Laptop\Downloads\*.glb`. All 7 SCP'd at 100% (a couple "Permission denied, please try again" were just mistyped passwords, retried successfully).

### 15c. URDF + ArmViewer3D wiring
Claude Code on the Jetson: built/validated `models/robots/estun_s10-140/s10-140.urdf` (6 revolute joints; manual+drawing dims from §10b/§14 — base 186 / 700 / 700 / offsets 221/175 / wrist 161.5/150.5 / reach 1400; limits J1,2,4,5,6 ±360°, J3 ±160°; vel 150/180°/s); copied GLBs + URDF into the frontend public dir; uses `urdf-loader` with the GLTFLoader callback (per §10b) so .glb loads with baked materials; animates J1–J6 from the WebSocket `joint_positions` (radians) with lerp smoothing; kept OrbitControls + camera presets (Front/Side/Top/Iso) + joint readout panel. **STATUS: deployed; meshes confirmed served (200 / model/gltf-binary) via curl probes.**

## 16. HTTPS URL TRANSITION — RECURRING SUPPORT POINT
The dashboard is now TLS-only on :8080 (from the v15 HTTPS work). Repeatedly surfaced this session:
- Correct URL is **`https://192.168.1.246:8080`** (the `s` is the only difference). First visit per device shows "Your connection is not private" (self-signed cert) → Advanced → Proceed once. This is expected on a LAN self-signed cert, not actually unsafe.
- **A single TCP socket speaks either TLS or plain HTTP, not both** — so `http://...:8080` cannot work while :8080 is TLS-only. Options on record: (1) move HTTPS off 8080 + serve an http→https redirect on 8080 (~10-min change; every bookmark/PWA/wss URL must re-point to the new HTTPS port e.g. 8443); (2) disable HTTPS (reverts the camera-over-HTTP block — rejected); (3) live with the https:// URL (chosen). Decision retained from v15: keep 8080, use https://.
- **PWA / kiosk gotcha:** a home-screen PWA pinned to the old `http://` URL shows ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE forever; must open Chrome → new https:// URL → accept cert → re-install ("Add to Home screen"). For the KIOSK specifically, the Chromium kiosk launch URL/flags must be updated to https:// and accept the self-signed cert (e.g. `--ignore-certificate-errors` / `--unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure=https://192.168.1.246:8080`). Kiosk-URL fix prompt authored.

## 17. PROGRAM-FROM-DEMONSTRATION (PBD) — RUNTIME + API-KEY SAGA + STRATEGY

### 17a. Whisper/ffmpeg/python deps installed; API key required
PBD verification needs the understanding backend's API key. ffmpeg 4.4.2 installed; python deps installed in background (NOTE: pip upgraded click 8.1.8 → 8.4.1, violating ouster-sdk 0.16.2's `<8.2.0` pin — Ouster is blocked at the physical layer per prior memory so not in use; downgrade with `pip install 'click<8.2.0'` later if needed).

### 17b. API failure: 400 "balance too low" despite funded account — DIAGNOSTIC DISCIPLINE
PBD returned confidence 0 / no summary / "Anthropic API request failed. Error 400. Your balance is too low." User states the account is funded and that the money and the key are "in the same exact spot." This was NOT resolved by assertion — the **definitive isolation test** was prescribed and remains the gating action:
- Identify the EXACT key the `roboai-pbd` service uses at runtime (first-8/last-4 masked only; check systemd `Environment=`, env files under /opt/cobot + /home/teddy/cobot_ws, and `printenv`); flag if MULTIPLE conflicting keys exist (a stale one winning is the classic trap).
- Test THAT key directly against `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` with a trivial ping, bypassing project code. **200 ⇒ key fine, bug is in our code; 400 "balance too low" ⇒ key belongs to an UNFUNDED workspace/account (credits are per-WORKSPACE, not per-account — money and key can be in different workspaces of the same org, or different logins); 401 ⇒ invalid/revoked; 404 ⇒ wrong model string.**
- **STATUS: UNRESOLVED — pending the raw curl result.** Most-likely root cause on the table: the key physically on the Jetson differs from the funded key in the console (compare first8/last4 against console), or wrong workspace. Fix = put the funded-workspace key in ONE authoritative place (env file + systemd), remove duplicates, daemon-reload, restart, re-curl to 200. Never print the full key.

### 17c. Pro/Max vs API — CLARIFIED
Claude **Pro/Max subscription CANNOT be used by the PBD backend.** Pro/Max is for interactive human use (claude.ai, apps, and Claude Code dev auth); it carries no API key for application code. The PBD runtime is automated programmatic use → requires the metered API. Claude Code itself may run on the subscription for DEV work, but the PBD app cannot borrow that auth. Practical split: keep Pro/Max for Claude Code dev; fund the API for the PBD runtime (pennies per demonstration).

### 17d. LOCAL vs API — STRATEGY DECISION: "API now, go local later (teacher model)"
The PBD understanding layer is API-pluggable by design (`api_backend.py` active, `local_backend.py` stub, one-config switch). Whisper transcription is ALREADY local. **DECISION: use the API as the TEACHER now (high-quality understanding) while the learning store accumulates corrected (demonstration → corrected-program) pairs; fine-tune a small LOCAL model offline later and deploy to the Jetson to replace the API call.** Ollama (llama3.1:8b) is already in the stack as the eventual local path; honest caveat recorded: a local 8B will give noticeably lower understanding quality than the API for messy multi-step demonstrations until fine-tuned on the project's own corpus. The whole strategy depends on the learning store actually capturing the full per-demo record (raw clip, transcript, frames, API draft, HUMAN-CORRECTED version, backend provenance, cell_id) — verify the loop is closed or the API spend builds no corpus.

## 18. SETUP / COMMISSIONING WIZARD + CELL DATA MODEL (new, in Configure tab)

### 18a. Architecture decision — WHERE this belongs
A dedicated **Setup/Commissioning Wizard in the Configure tab**, SEPARATE from the per-task Program Wizard. Rationale: cell commissioning is RUN-ONCE-PER-CELL (rare, technical); task programming is FREQUENT (operator-facing). Mixing them would clutter and risk accidental baseline re-runs. The Setup Wizard establishes the known-world foundation; the Program Wizard operates within a chosen commissioned cell.

### 18b. Cell data model
- Stored at `/opt/cobot/cells/{cell_id}/profile.json`, `baseline_cloud.pcd`, and `/opt/cobot/cells/index.json`.
- Endpoints: GET/POST/PUT/DELETE `/api/cells`, `/api/cells/{id}`; `/api/cells/{id}/baseline` (+ `/status`); `/api/cells/active` + `/api/cells/{id}/activate`; `/api/cells/{id}/programs` (programs whose cell_id matches); `/api/cells/{id}/baseline/cloud` (stored cloud as JSON for rendering).

### 18c. CRITICAL ARCHITECTURE FACTS established this session (drove several redesigns)
- **The LiDAR (Livox MID-360) is mounted ON THE ROBOT BASE, fixed.** LiDAR-to-robot-base is a FIXED KNOWN TRANSFORM (a code constant — NOT operator-measured, NOT a wizard question). Robot base = world origin. → The "robot base position" wizard step was REMOVED; do not ask where the robot/LiDAR is.
- **Baseline scan is STATIONARY** (robot does not move during capture) — simple dense accumulation of `/lidar/points_dense`.
- This also clarifies the §earlier eye-in-hand discussion: that pertained to the future MotionCam (camera) mounting; the LiDAR itself is base-mounted.

### 18d. Final wizard step sequence (after iterative trimming)
1. **Name the cell.**
2. **Network & hardware check** (works now): LiDAR reachable (ping 192.168.1.150 + /lidar/points hz/points, observed ~60k pts · 7.7Hz on /ws/lidar), cam0/cam1 present, robot arm (red until arrival — expected, Next allowed).
3. **Environment baseline scan** (works now — core feature): stationary ~10s accumulation → voxel-downsample → save baseline_cloud.pcd; live progress/point-count/3D preview; capturing→saving→captured.
4. **Hand-eye calibration** — DISABLED placeholder ("Requires the MotionCam, arriving later"); Skip.
5. **Review & Save** → commissioning_complete=true, mark active.
- **REMOVED from the wizard:** the Workspace-Bounds step (see §19 — bounds were built, then removed from BOTH the wizard and the cell dropdown per user direction), the robot-base-position step (§18c), and the safety-zones step (user: "remove the safety zones question in the wizard").
- "Commission a New Cell" uses this STEPPED wizard. Existing cells list shows name, Complete/Incomplete badge, green-dot active, associated-program count.

### 18e. Two-wizard relationship + cell selection in Program Wizard
Program Wizard gained a FIRST step "Which workspace is this program for?" — card list of commissioned cells, defaulting to the ACTIVE cell; if none, a notice + shortcut to Configure but still proceedable. Saved program JSON gains a `cell_id`. Program Library shows a per-program cell pill/badge + a "Show programs for: [cell]" filter (including "(no cell assigned)" for legacy programs). Verified end-to-end (create cell → baseline captures REAL points → activate → new program pre-selects active cell → library shows pill/filter; backend curls confirm).

### 18f. EDIT behavior — single settings page, NOT the wizard
DECISION: "Commission a New Cell" = stepped wizard (creation). **EDIT on an existing cell opens a SINGLE consolidated editable settings page showing ALL wizard decisions at once** (name, hardware status w/ re-check, baseline viewer + recapture, hand-eye placeholder) — NOT the stepped flow. Standard pattern: guided flow for creation, flat settings page for editing. Per-section independent save via PUT; partial updates; saved-confirmation/dirty indicators. (A "Re-run Full Setup Wizard" link may remain, but EDIT itself must not launch the stepped flow.)

### 18g. Expandable cell dropdown (Configure)
Clicking a cell expands an editable detail panel (accordion, one open at a time): name/status/activate/delete; **Associated Programs** (open/edit/duplicate/remove-from-cell/move-to-another-cell, count, via /api/cells/{id}/programs); **Environment Baseline** (renders the SAVED PCD — not live — recapture inline, "Live vs Baseline" overlay); hand-eye placeholder; **Raw/Advanced TRIMMED** per user to ONLY the "Re-run Full Setup Wizard" button (removed: profile.json view, profile/baseline paths, cell_id display).

## 19. WORKSPACE BOUNDS — BUILT, THEN CIRCULARIZED, THEN REMOVED (full honest trail)
This feature went through three user-directed states in one session; recorded in full since nothing is removed from the MD:
1. **Rect/oriented box (built):** real baseline top-down (height-colored XY projection) as the backdrop; robot at center; dashed 1.4m REACH ring (S10-140 SR1400); a work box that DRAGS, RESIZES (corner handles), and ROTATES (yaw handle); two-way numeric binding (center X/Y, size X/Y, Z min/max, yaw°); corners outside the 1.4m ring turn red with "Box extends beyond robot reach"; per-section save; backward-compat for legacy flat {x_min..} bounds (converted to center+size+yaw on load). Worked in both the wizard step and the Edit page. **CAVEAT recorded:** once a box is rotated, the flat AABB is only an approximation of the rotated box — downstream consumers (safety zones, future background-subtraction) must read center/size/yaw_deg, NOT the flat AABB.
2. **Circularized (redesign):** because robot reach is RADIAL, bounds became a CIRCLE centered (auto-snapped) on the robot origin (NOT draggable — an off-center reach circle is physically meaningless); single adjustable Working Radius (≤1.4m max reach, clamped) + Z min/max only; removed all X/Y size/center/yaw controls; dashed 1.4m max-reach ring + solid translucent working circle; the captured baseline top-down shows THROUGH as the backdrop. Timing fix noted: during NEW-cell commissioning the baseline is captured mid-wizard, so the bounds step reads the just-captured cloud either from the saved endpoint OR from wizard Zustand state (no save round-trip dependency); explicit "Baseline scene not loaded" message instead of a silent blank.
3. **REMOVED (final state):** per user, the Workspace-Bounds STEP was removed from the "Commission a New Cell" wizard AND the Workspace-Bounds SECTION removed from the cell dropdown/Edit view. **Saved workspace_bounds data on existing cells is NOT deleted** — just no longer collected/displayed in the UI (backward compatibility preserved). Net: the wizard no longer collects bounds at all.

## 20. COLLISION DETECTION (built on baseline + existing lidar_perception + URDF)
Prompt authored/executed to add collision detection using the captured LiDAR scene, showing detected objects as bounding boxes in the robot 3D view, limited to the robot's range of motion:
- **Reuse** the existing `lidar_perception` pipeline (ground seg + DBSCAN clustering + bbox) — do NOT rewrite.
- **Detect** objects in the live cloud; FILTER to those intersecting the robot's 1.4m reach cylinder; optional baseline background-subtraction to flag static/known (permanent fixtures) vs new/dynamic — but BOTH remain collision hazards (a static bench can still be hit). Publish on `/collision/objects` (id, bbox, static/dynamic, min-distance-to-robot).
- **Robot volume** from /joint_states + URDF approximated as per-link CAPSULES (sphere-swept segments) — fast, no full mesh collision needed. Min distance robot-capsules ↔ object boxes → CLEAR (>150mm) / WARNING (50–150mm) / COLLISION (<50mm), thresholds configurable.
- **3D scene viz:** status-colored boxes (green/yellow/red), static=dashed vs dynamic=solid, labels (id, distance mm, static/dynamic), the 1.4m boundary drawn, nearest-first list, overall banner (CLEAR/PROXIMITY WARNING/COLLISION RISK).
- **Safety integration:** feed collision status as an ADDITIONAL input to the existing safety/speed-scale mechanism — do NOT replace/weaken the existing proximity/safety_monitor. WARNING reduces speed scale, COLLISION stops; if unsure, publish status and flag rather than rewire.
- **Staged/testable now** with LiDAR + a static/last-commanded robot pose; auto-updates when /joint_states is live (arm arrives); optional mock-object toggle to verify green→yellow→red transitions.
- **HONEST CAVEAT:** this is real-time proximity DETECTION/warning + visualization (the correct first layer). True collision PREVENTION (swept-volume planning) eventually wants MoveIt2 (still pending; needs the official Estun URDF/DH per §11).

## 21. LIDAR — DENSE CLOUD RESTORED; FUSION DISABLED (root cause + correct fix)
LiDAR (Livox MID-360, IP 192.168.1.150; Jetson host 192.168.1.200 on eno1 via /32 SSH-safe host route) "not working" → diagnosed: the LiDAR + accumulator were fine (`/lidar/points_dense` ~66k pts @ ~7.7Hz). **Root cause: `roboai-fusion` was degrading to ~80–96 points (its cameras disabled, use_cam0/use_cam1=false) and that tiny fused cloud was TAKING DASHBOARD PRIORITY over the good dense cloud.**
- **User chose OPTION 1 (stop + disable fusion)** so the dashboard falls through to `/lidar/points_dense`. NOTE PROCESS POINT: Claude Code initially executed OPTION 3 (re-enable cameras in fusion) against the user's stated choice — corrected back to Option 1 (stop, disable, revert use_cam0/1 to false, confirm fused topic silent, confirm dashboard shows ~66k). Reinforces v15 lesson: do what was chosen, one fix.
- Likely systemic cause of "broke after reboot": the /32 host route doesn't survive reboot unless re-added by the service ExecStartPre (`ip addr add 192.168.1.200/32 dev eno1; ip route add 192.168.1.150/32 dev eno1`).
- Dense baseline viewer in the wizard improved: BRIGHTER points + THICKER/larger points within the 1.4m reach (distance-based point sizing, or two point layers split at 1.4m XY radius); parameterized so shared point-cloud components elsewhere don't change unintentionally.

## 22. 3D VIEW FRAME MISMATCH — LiDAR/objects not appearing where the robot is
BUG: objects/points render fine in the "Cameras & LiDAR" view but NOT in the robot 3D view. Diagnostic-first prompt authored (do not guess): compare DATA SOURCE (same topic/WS?), COORDINATE FRAME (ROS Z-up vs three.js Y-up — the working view may apply a conversion the robot view doesn't), SCALE/UNITS (meters vs mm; URDF/GLB import scale; camera frustum/clip), ORIGIN alignment (robot base vs cloud center), and RENDER LAYER (is a points object actually in the robot view's scene graph?). Strongest hypotheses: (1) Z-up→Y-up axis convention applied inconsistently, or (2) unit/scale mismatch collapsing the cloud to a speck or pushing it outside the frustum. Match the robot view to the known-good Cameras&LiDAR view; ensure collision bboxes render in the correct frame. Report root cause before fixing.

## 23. PBD WIZARD FULL-SCREEN / NO-CLIP FIX (tablet)
PBD wizard was clipped top/bottom (worst on tablet). Fix deployed: full-screen shell using **100dvh** (not 100vh — 100vh includes mobile address bar and overflows), flex column with fixed header + **flex:1 body with min-height:0 and overflow-y:auto** (the critical flex-child scroll gotcha — without min-height:0 the body won't shrink and pushes the footer/Generate button off-screen, exactly the "can't reach buttons" symptom) + pinned footer; safe-area insets; box-sizing border-box. Confirmed on laptop + tablet: header/footer pinned, long review step scrolls, Generate/Accept/Cancel always reachable. (SetupWizard + other modals untouched — separate scaffold.) Note: the wizard now shows API errors reachably IN the body (the 400 lands in the banner) — it will show real task summary + non-zero confidence once §17b is resolved.

## 24. CAMERA / PERCEPTION STRATEGY — NVIDIA STACK STATUS + DETECTING THE USER'S OWN PARTS
Reconfirmed from the MD what NVIDIA components are LIVE vs dormant (May 27 status): **Isaac ROS NITROS GPU detection pipeline is OPERATIONAL at ~17.9Hz on cam0 (COCO-80 only); YOLOv8n TRT engine 86.4 FPS @ 640² FP16; both D435i at 30Hz.** So "use the NVIDIA stack?" is moot — it's already the live detection path. nvblox is built but NOT yet wired to the dashboard; FoundationPose evaluated/on-device with the deferred volume-bias issue; **NanoOWL (open-vocabulary) PLANNED, not installed.**
- **CRITICAL GAP:** YOLOv8 detects only COCO-80 classes — it will NOT detect the user's industrial parts (e.g. BT225 bracket, delrin block). 
- **User goal: detect MY industrial parts.** Three honest paths laid out: (A) **NanoOWL** open-vocabulary text-prompt detection — fast, no training, but COARSE (good for "a bracket-like object is here," weak at distinguishing BT225L24 vs L28); (B) **custom-trained YOLO** — reliable 2D classification, needs hundreds of labeled images/part + offline GPU training (weeks; this is the fleet-learning data flywheel + where API auto-labeling fits); (C) **PPF+ICP recognition stack** — the commercial answer for IDENTITY + 6DOF PICK pose, CAD-driven (STEP files in hand), reference/CAD→model side buildable NOW with no camera (~30-40%), live matching needs the MotionCam's dense data.
- **User chose to first pair NanoOWL with the D435i.** HONEST verdict recorded: NanoOWL+D435i is a NATURAL fit (NanoOWL is an RGB detector → cam0 color feed; aligned depth gives APPROXIMATE 3D position) and a real step up from generic COCO (you can finally prompt for your parts). BUT the D435i is the weak link — sparse/coarse depth (MD: "marginal on sparse D435i data") — so the readback 3D is "roughly where," NOT pick-grade 6DOF pose. It is the AWARENESS layer, not the picking layer; picking still needs PPF+ICP + a structured-light camera. Also must tolerate the documented intermittent **cam0 freeze** (RealSense USB timeout; fixed by `systemctl restart roboai-cameras`) — detect stale frames (>2s), surface a "camera stalled" status, recover automatically; never show a stale frame as live.
- **Auto-label flywheel reaffirmed (NOT training the API):** calling the API to label hard/low-confidence crops generates (image→label) pairs for NeuRobots's OWN local YOLO corpus — local-only store, removable backend, never the provider's training. (Gated on §17b key fix.)
- **NanoOWL build prompt authored:** check/install NanoOWL for JetPack6/CUDA12.6 (NVIDIA-AI-IOT/nanoowl) + build the OWL-ViT TRT engine in tmux (long); ROS2 `nanoowl_node` on /cam0/color/image_raw with a LIVE-EDITABLE text-prompt list, depth-lookup approx 3D (labeled "approx (D435i)"), publish /perception/openvocab_detections; dashboard panel (typeable prompts → boxes in a distinct color from Isaac/COCO, confidence + approx distance, enable/disable toggle since NanoOWL is heavier than YOLO, camera-stalled indicator); keep Isaac/COCO running alongside (additive). Expectation set: NanoOWL is a vision-language transformer → lower FPS than the 17.9Hz Isaac pipeline even with TRT; sample frames if needed; report real FPS. Install is finicky on JP6 — STOP-and-report on failure rather than half-installing. **STATUS: PENDING run/verify (and whether cameras are physically live + achieved FPS).**

## 25. NVIDIA-STACK GUIDANCE (consolidated)
USE NVIDIA where already in use and where it earns its keep on the Orin: Isaac ROS NITROS GPU detection (live), nvblox 3D reconstruction (built; wire to dashboard is a pending nicety), FoundationPose for 6DOF pose (deferred volume-bias fix). KEEP plain YOLOv8+TensorRT as the detection runtime (don't re-architect onto Isaac DNN nodes for marginal benefit). KEEP recognition (PPF+ICP) IN-HOUSE as platform IP (deliberate v15 decision — "we built our own recognition"). Reaffirmed process caution from the MD: don't reach for a bigger framework to escape a bug — diagnose the actual failure (wiring/camera/deploy), per the twice-recorded vision-saga lesson.

## 27. PROCESS LESSONS — JUNE 16 ADDITIONS (extend §13; all prior lessons still govern)

Don't let a working awareness demo imply the picking/prevention problem is solved (§20, §24).
